newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares slip, seen treading water.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares slip, seen treading water.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased on Tuesday, pulled down by a fall in SKB bank, and traders forecast shares would remain range-bound over the short term.
"Liquidity is very low at the moment and in such a situation it is hard to forecast any significant moves in the short-term," said Bogdan Pusnik of brokers Medvesek Pusnik.
The SBI index fell 8.92 points or 0.66 percent to 1,334.94.
Overall nine shares fell and seven rose, while 11 were untraded. Turnover jumped to 82.9 million tolars from 39.2 million.
SKB had the highest turnover, falling 0.89 percent to 50,000 tolars on volume of 491 shares for total turnover of 24.6 million tolars.
Brokerage Primofin led the day's decliners, tumbling 8.33 percent to 13,200 tolars on volume of 12 shares.
Brokerage Dadas was the top gainer, jumping 8.59 percent to 8,090 tolars, but volume was very low at just five shares. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
